Sourdough fermentation relies on a symbiotic culture of wild yeasts (predominantly Saccharomyces and Kazachstania spp.) and lactic acid bacteria (LAB, primarily Lactobacillus and Leuconostoc spp.). The process involves two (2) fermentation pathways: (1) homofermentative (producing primarily lactic acid, yielding a mild flavor profile) and (2) heterofermentative (producing both lactic and acetic acid plus CO2, yielding a more complex, tangy flavor). Starter culture hydration level affects microbial balance; stiffer starters (50-60% hydration) favor acetic acid production, while liquid starters (100%+ hydration) favor lactic acid. Optimal fermentation temperature ranges from 24-28C for balanced flavor development (lower temperatures, i.e., 4-10C, slow fermentation and favor acetic acid accumulation during cold retardation). Final dough pH should measure between 3.8-4.2 for proper crumb structure. Gluten network development (assessed via the windowpane test) requires adequate mixing time (typically 10-15 min by hand or 6-8 min in a spiral mixer at speed 2). Bulk fermentation duration varies from 4-12 hrs depending on starter activity and ambient temperature.
